first.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the self-serve funnel, and memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value) is the most upstream lever, since completion feeds activation. I am verifying memory_86 and memory_91 because they are the two candidates I would actually choose between and both are the least independently corroborated; memory_86 is 24 days old and memory_91 only 15, but both were single consolidations and I want to see effect size, sample, and whether the lift was durable or a novelty bump before spending the only slot. I am deliberately NOT choosing promotional_pricing despite it being the direct answer to the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 explicitly records a material 30-day retention hit and an instruction not to generalize it, and the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not quarter-end acquisition. The competitive pressure is exactly the condition under which that guardrail is most tempting to override, which is why I am honoring it. Referral incentive (memory_57) is clean but targets established customers and does nothing for the two metrics that are actually falling; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment showing no distress. Key downstream risk to flag: onboarding/signup simplification (memory_31, memory_86) optimizes for completion and activation, which are proxies, not for QUALIFIED revenue. Stripping fields can raise activation while lowering lead quality and sales qualification signal, so the experiment must be scored on 30-day retention and qualified pipeline, not completion rate alone, or it reproduces the promotional-pricing failure mode in a subtler form. Uncertainty preserved: these memories are consolidated summaries from a pre-competitor market, and a 6% activation drop may be driven by a worse inbound mix from competitive poaching rather than by funnel friction, in which case a funnel fix will underperform its historical lift. Standard experiment scale with a holdout, not a broad rollout, until verification returns.
